title: The Policyholder gives Sky total control of an insurance vehicle while disclaiming legal affiliation with it
content:
A.2.9.1.2.1 creates the Policyholder to do what a protocol cannot: "[a]ct as a legal counterparty with insurance brokers, insurance, reinsurance, underwriters, or risk management companies" and "[a]ct as a policyholder of insurance contracts, which will have as beneficiaries participants of the Sky Ecosystem." Insurance requires a contracting legal person; the Policyholder supplies one so that risk can be transferred to third parties rather than merely self-insured.

The control list is comprehensive — Sky Governance "can designate and remove Directors, Supervisor, and Committees," "can instruct the entity to act and ratify decisions," and directors' power "is limited to administrative and operative roles." Then the same provision states the entity "will not manage Sky's assets nor will be legally affiliated with Sky."

That pairing is the interesting tension. Legally, this degree of direction is close to the classic test for control, and a counterparty or regulator examining the arrangement would have material grounds to treat the Policyholder as an instrumentality of Sky. The disclaimer of affiliation is asserted rather than structurally guaranteed by anything in the text.

The motive is clear enough — Sky wants insurance capacity without creating an entity whose liabilities or regulatory status attach back to the protocol. Whether "controlled but unaffiliated" survives contact with an adversarial party is the untested assumption the whole legal risk transfer layer rests on.

Status is early: setup and operating budget come out of the Resilience Fund budget "intended to move later to a separate budget," approval requires SKY holders to approve structure and costs via a Governance Poll (A.2.9.1.2.2), and A.2.9.1.2.3 records "no active Policyholders."
